summary: Radar for 2026-11-17, during ObesityWeek, 9 days before Thanksgiving. Following the playbook (broad long videos, Shorts on felt symptoms), there are 4 clear opportunities. (1) The holiday table on tirzepatide is the highest-momentum seasonal hook. Its search peak is 18–27 Nov, so the 20:00 Shorts should start on 11-18. (2) The FDA's class-wide NAION label change (announced 9 Nov) reached a second wave of mainstream coverage on 16 Nov (Yahoo Health, NJBIZ). The same day, the Washington Post ran "serious complications few know about". Together they make a natural hook for the queued "Serious Risks: How Rare?" long video. FDA figures from the trade press: about 6.4 vs 3.8 NAION events per 100,000 person-years, in a meta-analysis of 126 RCTs. Fact-check against the updated PI. (3) "Why don't GLP-1s work for everyone?" spread from The Conversation, BBC Science Focus and the GLP1R-variant paper into new real-world tirzepatide data. That is the fresh hook for "Weight Loss: How Much in the Trials?". (4) Foundayo has 3 fresh hooks: the oral vs injectable safety review (Endocrine, 16 Nov), the AFR report of a second weight-loss pill in Australia "within days", and the China approval. Together they refresh the queued Foundayo what-to-expect video. Evergreen search formats stay strong: Mounjaro vs Zepbound, Months 2–6, injection-site Shorts, travelling with the pen, hair loss and nausea. Emerging items that need caution: SURMOUNT-ADOLESCENTS (JAMA, 15 Nov; the paediatric story is spreading through the NYT and WUSA9), skin pain or dysesthesia (in case reports and a Medsafe notice; not on the US tirzepatide label), and heart rate (cohort data; the label supports it). Rejected: poison-control calls and unapproved drugs, retatrutide 'supplier' PR, 'staying on low doses' stories, 'GLP-1 booster' supplements, and pricing, FEHB and Medicaid stories.

candidates.topic: Thanksgiving on tirzepatide: feeling full fast, heartburn, drinks at the party, leftovers, and travelling with the pen (storage per the label)
candidates.angle: Holiday-table Shorts series, each one a felt moment ('full after 3 bites: is this normal?'). The answer is the label mechanism (slower stomach emptying) plus practical habits (protein first, smaller portions, eating slowly). Each Short logs the Thanksgiving long video as its target. No 'safe amount' of alcohol; the low-blood-sugar caveat applies only to people with diabetes on insulin or a sulfonylurea.

can you drink alcohol on mounjaro

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro/Zepbound) new eye warning: the FDA's class-wide NAION label change (announced 9 Nov), now in a second wave of mainstream coverage
candidates.angle: Label-change explainer. What the new Warnings and Precautions text says, how rare it is (FDA meta-analysis of 126 RCTs: about 6.4 vs 3.8 events per 100,000 person-years; verify against the updated PI), and the one thing to act on (sudden, painless vision loss in one eye means call right away). Calm, not scary. Name both NANOS and the AAO if cited. Best as a lead chapter of 'Serious Risks: How Rare?', plus one 'Is this normal?'-style Short.
candidates.why_now: The FDA announced it on 9 Nov. On 16 Nov, Yahoo Health, NJBIZ and Fox stations ran consumer explainers, so it is moving from trade press to the mainstream. Label-change formats beat our channel's usual views by 10–195x in this niche. Few tirzepatide-specific explainers exist; most say 'Ozempic'.
